newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI ENDS SHADE HIGHER, KESKO BOOSTS VOLUME.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI ENDS SHADE HIGHER, KESKO BOOSTS VOLUME.

text.p: Shares ended a shade higher on
Monday as gains in Swedish paper stocks and in U.S. forestries
in early trade helped forest shares higher, brokers said.
Trade was slow but the volume was boosted by a massive
in-house deal in wholesaler and retailer Kesko in the afternoon,
they said. Shares could extend gains on Tuesday since tone was
still strong after the Bank of Finland's key tender rate cut
last Friday. Kesko closed at 73.00 markka, down 1.80 markka or
more than two percent.
Telecoms group Nokia ended unchanged at 185.00 markka after
moderate trade.
Merita closed 0.05 markka lower at 9.69 after hitting a
two-week low 9.61 markka in quiet trade.
"Merita is sliding amid a lack of confidence," a broker
said. He referred to Merita's January-June report released on
August 6, which showed improved profits but no recovery in net
income from financial operations.
Consumer goods group Fiskars ended fair trade at a new
year-high 303.00 markka, up 13.00 markka, after
higher-than-expected January-June profits, but foodstuffs group
Atria lost 1.50 markka to 47.00 on lower first-half profits.
-- Helsinki newsroom +358-0-6805 0248
